thread.subject: [BUG] bitland-mifs-wmi: Power profiles not working on Xiaomi Mi NoteBook Ultra

CAEX=435pEyPHPjJgQnJUJLL8JJD65RsRa7Sjbx4.subject: [BUG] bitland-mifs-wmi: Power profiles not working on Xiaomi Mi NoteBook Ultra

blocks.text: Hello,

I'm running Fedora with Linux kernel 7.1.8 on my Xiaomi Mi NoteBook Ultra,
and the new bitland-mifs-wmi driver loaded automatically for my system.

i run
cat /sys/firmware/acpi/platform_profile_choices it gives output
low-power balanced balanced-performance performance

If I try to switch to Performance mode (echo performance >
/sys/firmware/acpi/platform_profile), I get an error: Operation not
supported.
If I try to switch to Quiet mode (echo low-power >
/sys/firmware/acpi/platform_profile), it doesn't give an error, but it
silently fails. If I check the file immediately after, it still says
balanced.
I have attached my dmidecode output and my ACPI tables (acpidump) in case
you want to look at my hardware's specific implementation.
(and also an AI analysis if u want to look otherwise forget it)
Please let me know if there's any testing I can do to help get this model
supported!
Thanks for your work on the driver.

lines.text: I unloaded |redmi_wmi| but the issue is still not resolved.
Regarding the patch: for testing it, do I only need to compile the > driver module itself, or do I need to build the full kernel? Sorry for > the beginner question.

blocks.text: You need to compile the entire kernel.
By the way, for speeding up the build, you could run:
make localmodconfig
to generate a kernel config that suit your machine.
Then run the following commands to build and install the kernel:
make -j$(nproc) && sudo make modules_install && sudo make install

blocks.text: Those patches were written with AI assistance, and I do not have a Xiaomi or Redmi laptop on hand.
I believe further reverse engineering work is required.

I made a mistake in the patches, the DMI vendor of Xiaomi devices are not "Xiaomi", please change it to "TIMI" (from your dmidecode.txt attachment) and retest the driver. (or use patch v6 that I sent to the mailing list)
